title: Builder

act2.summary: a new optional stage, and a rule spanning it and an existing one

solutions.title: QuoteBuilder: mutable stages over one state object, one validation pass in build()
solutions.tradeoff: Every business rule lives in exactly one method, checked after every field has its final value, regardless of what order the chain called its stages in - a new rule spanning two fields is one line in build(), not a line duplicated into each field's own stage. The price: a class holding mutable state instead of a chain of small immutable drafts, and two callers holding the same draft reference can now surprise each other, since a stage mutates in place rather than handing back a fresh value.

reviewFocus: Does build() check every business rule after all fields are set, or does any stage still validate before every field has its final value?
Does any rule in build() depend on which order the chain's stages were called in - and if not, why not?
Is startQuote's job now just opening a builder over the required fields, with no business logic of its own?

What happens if a caller keeps an earlier draft reference around and calls a stage on it after already calling build() once - does the pattern route behave the same as a persistent, immutable draft would? See WALKTHROUGH.md's 'What it cost'.
Is the walkthrough honest that act 2 measured a tie, not a win - same files, same lines, same hunks - and that this is evidence for a different argument than 'the pattern is cheaper to extend'?
